clue.text: Church might well have this set aside

definitions.text: Church might well have this set aside

parts.words: Church might well have this set aside
parts.note: a cross-shaped church has an arm set to each side of the nave, so the feature is literally placed at the side

explanation.surface: A congregation might put something away for later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set aside' looks like saving, but it describes architecture: the part of a church that projects to the side of the main body.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the crosswise arm of a cruciform church, lying at the side of the nave.

clue.text: Note sailor and soldier need a weekend rest from duty

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
AB is an able-bodied seaman
RE is the Royal Engineers, standing in for a soldier
the end of the word week is K

explanation.surface: Military staff needing a couple of days off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weekend' gives the last letter of week, K. A break for a hot drink at work is a British institution.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pause from work for refreshments is a break from duties.

clue.text: Taken on and taken off without reason

annotationWithheld.why: Taken on and taken off without reason (9): 'Taken on' defines APPOINTED, but no sound parse of 'taken off without reason' gives the letters.
annotationWithheld.clue: Taken on and taken off without reason

clue.text: Beastly accommodation — the Continental kind

parts.note: a sty is housing for pigs
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Living like animals, in the European manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Continental' means 'the' in a European language, here French LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A manner or type of something is a style, as in a sort.

clue.text: Soothe the head about state set-up

indicators.note: the word for head goes around the reversed state

parts.note: pate is the head

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the abbreviation is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: CAL is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: Calming the boss over the way the country is organised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The head' looks like a school head teacher, but it is the top of the skull; 'set-up' works upwards because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To appease or pacify someone is to calm them down.

clue.text: Where soldiers can take a dip

definitions.text: Where soldiers can take a dip

parts.words: Where soldiers can take a dip
parts.note: soldiers here are strips of toast that are dipped into a soft-boiled egg at breakfast

explanation.surface: Troops looking for a spot to go swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'soldiers' are fingers of buttered toast dunked into a boiled egg; the dip happens in the cup that holds the egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A small breakfast holder keeps a boiled egg upright so toast fingers can be dunked into it.

clue.text: Material read, begin work

indicators.note: the words are worked into a new order, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to read the brief and start on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' rearranges READ BEGIN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a hard-wearing twill fabric used for coats.

clue.text: Honour a member's appeal

parts.note: CH is the Companion of Honour, a British honour
an arm is a member, or limb, of the body

explanation.surface: A club member asking to be decorated.
explanation.walkthrough: CH stands for Companion of Honour, an award in the British honours system.
explanation.definitionFit: Attractiveness or allure is a winning quality.

clue.text: … as in principle a secretary must do

definitions.text: … as in principle a secretary must do

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words principle a secretary, spanning the word breaks

explanation.surface: Ideally, an assistant has to keep the boss happy.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry on from 7 Down's 'appeal'; the letters run across PRINCIPLE A SECRETARY, and the whole clue says what a secretary must do.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretary is expected to satisfy the employer, and the word also completes an appeal.

clue.text: A fat goat?

definitions.meaning: a dairy spread made from cream
a goat butts, so it is one who butts

explanation.surface: Asking whether a plump goat is the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Butter is a dairy fat, and a goat is jokingly one that butts with its horns.

clue.text: Give employment to a page and keep busy

parts.note: to ply is to work steadily at something

explanation.surface: Hiring a young page and making sure the lad is never idle.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something to use is to employ it, as in using a skill.

clue.text: Suggest a simple reprimand

parts.note: simple in the sense of slow-witted means dumb
to rate is an old verb meaning to scold

explanation.surface: Proposing that a mild telling-off would do.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE as 'scold' is an older sense the solver may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: To foreshadow or hint at something faintly is to suggest it.

clue.text: May be in retreat or going on and on

indicators.note: the letters may be arranged into another word, so these words are the material to be reworked

explanation.surface: Either a soldier in withdrawal, or someone droning endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May be' signals that IN RETREAT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repeating itself over and over is persistently continuing, like a refrain.

clue.text: They're inclined to get people down

definitions.text: They're inclined to get people down

parts.words: They're inclined to get people down
parts.note: inclined means sloping rather than disposed, and getting people down means letting them descend rather than depressing them

explanation.surface: Gloomy folk who tend to depress everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints pessimists; the real reading is of sloping walkways for descending.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping surfaces join two levels, letting people go down without steps.

clue.text: Possibly the leader will make it clear

indicators.note: the following words will be made into something new, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editorial writer promising to clarify matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' is a grammatical example (the definite article) and a leader is a newspaper's leading piece; 'will make' rearranges IT CLEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The' is the definite one in grammar, and a newspaper's leader is a written piece of its kind.

clue.text: Awfully decent — not relaxed though

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are mangled, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone frightfully nice but never at ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges DECENT and NOT; 'though' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfied and at peace means calm and at ease.

clue.text: Such fruit is available in the fall

indicators.note: the word is goes inside the word for what falls from the sky

parts.note: rain is what falls from the sky

explanation.surface: Fruit you can only buy in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The fall' looks like autumn, the American season, but here it is rainfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Dreamers who are thought heels

parts.note: an idea is a thought
a ship heels or lists when it leans over

explanation.surface: Visionaries who are thought to be cads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heels' looks like scoundrels, but it is the verb for a ship leaning over.
explanation.definitionFit: People with lofty, unrealistic visions are fanciful visionaries.

clue.text: Hard-working bosses accepting financial commitment

indicators.note: the bosses take the debt note inside them

parts.note: bosses are raised studs, as on a shield
an IOU is a written promise to pay

explanation.surface: Diligent managers taking on a debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bosses' looks like managers, but it means raised knobs or studs.
explanation.definitionFit: Diligent in study and application means hard at work.

clue.text: Good-looker in a party about to fall from grace

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: about turns the word for a moral lapse round

parts.note: to sin is to fall from grace

explanation.surface: A handsome guest at a party on the point of disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns SIN into NIS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this beautiful youth became the byword for a handsome man.

clue.text: Well of course!

parts.note: well here is a spring, and course is a river's course, so this is where a river rises

explanation.surface: An exclamation meaning naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a shrug; read 'well' as a spring and 'course' as a watercourse. The letters of COURSE also rearrange to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The spring where a stream rises is its origin.

clue.text: The reason given for writing beforehand?

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
text is written matter

explanation.surface: Asking why something was written ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the word as PRE-TEXT, writing that comes before.
explanation.definitionFit: An excuse put forward to cover the real motive is a stated reason.

clue.text: Getting quietly back on a horse

parts.note: P is piano, quietly in music
astern means backwards, at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Climbing back on the horse in silence.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stands for a part found on a horse: the area between fetlock and hoof.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the part of a horse's leg between the fetlock and the hoof.

clue.text: Hound an individual behaving stupidly in punt

indicators.note: the fool goes inside the wager

parts.note: a punt is a bet
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone making a fool of themselves in a flat-bottomed boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punt' looks like the boat poled along English rivers, but it is a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a short-legged breed of hunting dog.

clue.text: Returning after midday in drink is great!

indicators.note: the reversed time goes inside the beer

parts.note: ale is a drink

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for afternoon is read backwards

parts.note: PM stands for post meridiem, after midday

explanation.surface: A drinker toasting the afternoon pint as wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After midday' stands for the abbreviation for afternoon, and 'Returning' turns it round before it goes into the beer; the exclamation hides the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plentiful or abundant means large in amount, which is close to great.

clue.text: Something that irritates a woman undergoing fitness training

indicators.note: in a down clue the woman goes under the training

parts.note: PE is physical education
Eve is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman doing exercises and finding it annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet hate is a source of annoyance.

clue.text: Somewhat anxious, not having been paid

explanation.surface: A worker fretting because the wages have not arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsettled means mildly uneasy, and also describes a bill that remains outstanding.

clue.text: Shylock's friend referring to a pipe

definitions.meaning: a character in The Merchant of Venice

explanation.surface: Shylock's companion talking about smoking.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubal is Shylock's fellow moneylender in The Merchant of Venice, and the adjective relates to a tube.

clue.text: Display just a single glass?

definitions.meaning: glasses are ..., so one lens would be a singular one

explanation.surface: Showing off with only a solitary drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a striking show, and jokingly one lens of a pair of glasses.

clue.text: Perch round the singer

parts.note: a perch is a fish of the bass family
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A bird sitting near a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perch' looks like a bird's seat but is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass voice, or one who sings with it, is a type of vocalist.

clue.text: Die in the attempt to be modish!

indicators.note: the word for dying goes inside the word for an attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
to die is to end

explanation.surface: Being fashionable even if it kills you.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashionable and up to date means in vogue.

clue.text: Breakdown specialists

parts.note: breakdown means examining something in parts, or a nervous collapse treated by a psychiatrist, rather than a car repair

explanation.surface: Roadside mechanics who fix cars.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests motoring recovery; these specialists break data down or treat mental breakdowns.
explanation.definitionFit: Experts who examine things part by part, or psychotherapists, deal in breakdowns.
